title: Learned diffusion-MRI enhancement changes migraine-group statistical contrasts
summary: Fourteen learned reconstruction methods were evaluated on scans from 50 episodic and 50 chronic migraine patients after training data from healthy controls. Improved recovery of group-difference voxels also introduced differences absent from the fuller-sampling reference. This is a bounded reconstruction audit, not proof that the added voxels are biologically false.
ai_technology: CNNs, U-Nets, denoising autoencoders, SARDI-Net and Swin Transformer reconstruction
organization: Universidad de Valladolid; Cardiff University; University of Rochester

evidence.tested: Training data comprised 60 healthy controls with 61-direction diffusion MRI; 14 participating methods reconstructed maps from 21-direction input for 50 episodic and 50 chronic migraine patients, whose group identities were hidden from participating teams. Identical TBSS analysis compared reconstructed group contrasts with the organizers’ 61-direction silver-standard contrast maps. New recovered reference-positive voxels and reference-negative significant voxels covaried across methods, with reported R-squared values .907 for axial diffusivity and .749 for mean diffusivity.
evidence.unknown: False positive here means significant after reconstruction but absent from the 61-direction statistical reference; this is not an independent biological ground truth or a clinical diagnostic false-positive rate. Differences concern 100 migraine patients under one acquisition setting and training on a different clinical group; the paper explicitly disallows generalization to all imaging tasks. Methods used heterogeneous training/validation arrangements, including synthetic training and model-selection differences. The reference-derived registration and skeleton were shared across comparisons. Image-quality improvement does not establish preservation of inferential conclusions, and the associations across 14 methods do not establish a universal numerical law.
evidence.ai_role: Trained reconstruction networks transformed reduced-direction diffusion data or its derived measures. The qualifying result is the source-specific effect of those learned transformations on measured clinical-group statistical contrasts, not a ranking of generic image-quality metrics.

source_review.scope: Original primary computational Methods, cohort/reference definitions, represented Results and bounded limitations actually read; no code executed or independent reanalysis.
